deep.reconstruction:
The page has two unrelated parts: a short algebraic fragment at top left, and a set of sexagesimal reduction computations, mostly in the right half. A vine-and-flower pencil doodle runs across the sheet. The previous page has Sun/Moon timing data and the next page a currency conversion; neither connects to this page.

(A) ALGEBRAIC FRAGMENT (top left). The heading reads roughly 'M R, R, r, R^theta(?)'. The three lines are:
(1) [r,R]^mu = A[1,R^mu] + B[r,R^mu]
(2) [r,R]·[1,R^mu] = [r,R^{mu+1}]{1 + R^{-mu} + R^{-2mu}}
(3) = [r,R^{mu+1}]·[1,R^mu]
The bracket [x,Q] is a two-argument function of a quantity and a 'base' raised to a power. This is reminiscent of Gauss's finite or infinite q-products and q-sums, as in 'Summatio quarumdam serierum singularium' (1808) and the Nachlass q-series papers. Line (1) asks how a power of [r,R] decomposes linearly over brackets with base R^mu. Comparing (2) with (3) shows that Gauss is using {1+R^{-mu}+R^{-2mu}} as the value of [1,R^mu] in some three-term (cubic?) case. Taken literally, (2)=(3) then just restates that, and dividing by [1,R^mu] would give [r,R]=[r,R^{mu+1}]. So the fragment is either an abandoned trial or uses a convention not recoverable from this page. The definition of the bracket is not given, and I do not attempt a reconstruction beyond this. The isolated numbers 209, 9973, 31784, 1882 are unexplained.

(B) STAR-PLACE REDUCTIONS. Each block has the form: catalogue position + precession (several minutes of arc) = mean place, then + two corrections of order 10-25" (evidently aberration and nutation, or the day-number terms) = apparent place.

Block 1 (my identification: gamma Lyrae):
- RA: 282°51'53.6" + 4'44.04" = 282°56'37.64".
- Then +23.1" +9.4" gives 282°57'10.14"; further +0.3" and +0.7" give ...11.14".
- Dec: 32°25'31.2" + 38.03" = 32°26'9.23".
- Then -2.2" +6.9" gives ...13.9"; +0.5" is noted.
- Check (mine): annual precession at alpha≈283°, delta≈32.4° is m + n sin(a) tan(d) ≈ 46.08 - 12.4 ≈ 33.7"/yr in RA and n cos(a) ≈ 4.46"/yr in Dec.
- 284.04"/33.7 ≈ 8.4 yr and 38.03"/4.46 ≈ 8.5 yr, so both terms are consistent with about 8.4 years of precession.
- Back-precessing gamma Lyrae (J2000 RA 284.74°, Dec +32°41') by about 190 years gives roughly RA 283°, Dec +32°27'. This matches.

Block 2 (my identification: beta Cygni / Albireo):
- RA: 290°39'49.9" + 5'6.32" = 290°44'56.22".
- Then +21.4" +11.2" = 290°45'28.82".
- Dec: 27°32'58.5" + 56.91" = 27°33'55.41".
- Then -3.2" +7.8" is listed; the total, 27°34'0.01", is not written.
- Precession rates of about 36.3"/yr in RA and 7.1"/yr in Dec give about 8.4 and 8.0 years respectively.
- Albireo (J2000 RA 292.68°, Dec +27°57.6') back-precessed about 190 years gives RA ≈ 290.8°, Dec ≈ 27°33'. This matches.

Block 3 (my identification: probably alpha Sagittae):
- RA: 292°47'18.80" + 5'39.63" (more likely 5'39.83"), then +19.9" +11.62" = 292°53'30.15".
- Converted to time this is 19h31m34s, which is the '19 31 34' written below. 292°53'30"/15 = 19h31m34.0s, which I verified.
- A 5'39.8" precession over about 8.4 yr implies about 40.4"/yr. That fits a star at RA ≈ 292.9°, Dec ≈ +17-18°, i.e. alpha Sagittae back-precessed to about 1810.

Interpretation: the three stars share an interval of about 8.4 years. This suggests mean places from a catalogue of epoch about 1800 being brought to about 1808-1812, with aberration and nutation added to give apparent places. These are presumably comparison stars for a comet or planet observation.

Other items:
- 51°32'20.3" - 51°25'57.1" = 6'23.2". Checked; this is of the order of Göttingen's latitude, about 51°32'.
- 51°32'20.8" - 28°20'17.2" = 23°12'3.6" (a zenith distance or colatitude-type difference). Checked.
- 23°27'49.4" is the obliquity of the ecliptic. The modern mean-obliquity formula gives 23°27'50.4" for 1810, so this value points to about 1810-1813.
- The expression 'alpha + beta cos(delta) + gamma sin(delta)' is the generic form of a declination-dependent correction, such as instrument constants or the day-number reduction in declination.
- 34°27'41.0" with -8.05, -0.50, -6.48 is a further reduction left uncompleted.
- 31.56, 32.00, 64.00 sum to 127.56, and 127.56/4 = 31.89; this is a weighted mean in which 32.00 counts twice.
- Scattered small sums (268.16, 15.58, 35.68, 2.35; 4008/2=2004; 3332-176-...) are unexplained.
errors: Block 3: with 5'39.63" as transcribed, 292°47'18.80" + 5'39.63" + 19.9" + 11.62" = 292°53'29.95", not 30.15". The 0.20" discrepancy disappears if the precession is read 5'39.83", so this is most likely a misreading or a slight slip.
Dec of block 2: the corrections -3.2" and +7.8" are listed but the result (27°34'0.01") is not written; the block is unfinished.

Algebraic fragment: if {1+R^-mu+R^-2mu} is [1,R^mu], then line (2) = line (3) is trivially consistent. However, cancelling gives [r,R]=[r,R^{mu+1}], which cannot hold generally. The fragment is incomplete or rests on an unstated definition and cannot be verified.
34°27'41.0" with corrections -8.05", -0.50", -6.48" has no total written (it would be 34°27'25.97").
Dec precession of block 2 (56.91", about 8.0 yr) is slightly inconsistent with its RA precession (about 8.4 yr). This is probably due to proper motion or rounded rate constants rather than an error.

results.what: Reduction of catalogue star positions to apparent place: precession added, then aberration and nutation corrections, for about three stars (probably gamma Lyr, beta Cyg, alpha Sge) at an epoch about 8.4 yr after the catalogue epoch
results.modern_name: reduction from mean to apparent place (precession, aberration, nutation; day numbers)
results.usually_credited_to: Bradley (aberration 1729, nutation 1748); systematized by Bessel (Tabulae Regiomontanae 1830)

results.what: Conversion of right ascension from arc to time: 292°53'30" = 19h31m34s

results.modern_name: possibly q-series / q-product (or Gaussian-sum) manipulations; definition unclear

deep.surprise_reason: Almost all of the page is routine astronomical reduction arithmetic of the kind Gauss did constantly around 1808-1813. The algebraic fragment is too short and undefined to establish any non-trivial result.

checkable.asserts: with precession read as 5'39.83" the block-3 sum equals 292°53'30.15" (should be 0; with 5'39.63" the result is -1/5)
RA and Dec precession of block 1 imply nearly the same elapsed time (about 8.4 vs 8.5 yr; difference small)

transcription_corrections: '5.39,63' in block 3 is probably '5.39,83', which the written total 30,15 requires.
Line 2 of the algebra: the opening brace '{1+R^{-mu}+R^{-2mu}' has no closing brace; the left factor reads [r,R]·[1,R^mu].
'6.23,2' is 6'23.2" (difference of the two 51° values), not a separate quantity.
'19 31 34' at the bottom is the RA 292°53'30" converted to time (19h31m34s).
In the RA block of block 1, '57 10,14' is the minutes and seconds of 282°57'10.14", and the following '+0,3 / 0,7 / 11,14' carries this to 11.14".
Heading symbols 'M R  R  r  R tau theta' are uncertain; '18' and '15' are struck-out folio numbers.
